tasks.personal-social-wellbeing-t3: Topic: Personal and Social Well-being. Cover diversity, culture, religion, rights and responsibilities, and substance abuse awareness. Ask learners to identify respectful actions, match rights to responsibilities, explain why stereotypes are harmful, recognise healthy responses to peer pressure, and choose safe actions that protect individuals and communities.
tasks.physical-education-t3: Topic: Physical Education. Cover athletics, relays, indigenous games, flexibility, and reaction time. Ask learners to identify safe warm-up and cool-down habits, recognise correct relay and jumping technique, explain teamwork and fair play, and choose actions that improve flexibility, coordination, and quick response in movement activities.
tasks.creative-arts-t3: Topic: Creative Arts. Cover South African cultural art, mixed media, choral verse, singing, and movement. Ask learners to identify respectful use of cultural themes, recognise mixed-media materials and texture, and answer questions about rehearsal, timing, expression, and group performance in integrated creative activities.
tasks.gr6-caring-for-animals-t3: Topic: Caring for animals for Grade 6 Life Skills (CAPS term 3 Personal and Social Well-being). Cover acts of cruelty to animals (hurting, neglect, abandoning, chaining in the sun), what a pet needs (food, clean water, shelter, exercise, a vet and vaccinations), that a pet is a long responsibility, protecting animals by telling a trusted adult who can report to the SPCA or the police, places of safety (the SPCA, animal shelters, wildlife centres), and staying safe around strange animals. Write for 11 to 12 year olds with no graphic detail.
tasks.gr6-caring-for-people-t3: Topic: Caring for people for Grade 6 Life Skills (CAPS term 3). Cover that every person has needs and views, noticing needs and listening to views, saying your own needs and views calmly and kindly without hurting others (an 'I feel... when... I need...' sentence), acts of kindness (small acts without a reward, such as sharing, helping a neighbour or including a lonely child), and kindness in the community including Mandela Day (67 minutes). Write for 11 to 12 year olds.
tasks.gr6-nation-building-heritage-t3: Topic: Nation-building and cultural heritage for Grade 6 Life Skills (CAPS term 3). Cover what nation, cultural heritage and nation-building mean, how cultural heritage unites a nation, the national symbols (the flag, first flown on 27 April 1994 with six colours; the anthem that joins Nkosi Sikelel' iAfrika and Die Stem and is sung in five languages; the coat of arms of 2000 with the motto !ke e: /xarra //ke meaning Diverse people unite), and the national days (Human Rights Day 21 March, Freedom Day 27 April, Africa Day 25 May, Mandela Day 18 July with 67 minutes, Women's Day 9 August, Heritage Day 24 September, Reconciliation Day 16 December, and Children's Day, which has no fixed date). Every date must be exactly as listed.
